turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class. Who decided that, and before or after anyone spoke to him?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
You reread them. And what did you find, Hale? I asked who decided on the zero, and I'm still waiting for that answer.
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
I'm not here to talk about how I raised my son. An impression isn't evidence, Hale. What is the basis for the zero?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Don't manage me, Hale. You still haven't told me what the zero rests on, and I'm writing down that you haven't.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
Then withdraw the zero, Hale. If we both care about him, that's the first thing you do, and it costs you nothing.
